title: Google Cloud Platform - A High level Overview of Data Catalog Service - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Data Catalog is a fully managed and scalable metadata management service. It allows organizations to quickly discover, manage and understand all their data in Google Cloud. It offers:

  • A simple and easy to use search interface for data discovery, powered by the same Google search technology that supports Gmail and Drive.
  • A flexible and powerful cataloging system for capturing technical and business metadata.
  • An auto-tagging mechanism for sensitive data with DLP API integration.

Note: Data Catalog is deprecated and is discontinued on June 1, 2026. Google Cloud has transitioned Data Catalog capabilities to Knowledge Catalog, formerly known as Dataplex Universal Catalog.

Core Components

Understanding the core components of Data Catalog helps organizations efficiently manage and explore their data assets.

1. Data Assets

Data assets are datasets and resources indexed in Data Catalog.

  • Includes supported resources such as BigQuery datasets and tables.
  • Stores metadata such as descriptions and schemas.
  • Enables discovery across projects and environments.

2. Search and Discovery

Data Catalog provides centralized search for locating relevant data assets.

  • Search using keywords, metadata, and resource information.
  • Filter results using available facets and attributes.
  • Helps users quickly find relevant datasets and tables.

3. Tag Templates

Tag templates provide structured metadata for organizing and classifying data.

  • Define reusable metadata fields.
  • Support data classification and governance.
  • Improve data documentation and discoverability.

4. Access Control Integration

Data Catalog works with the permissions of underlying data sources.

  • Respects existing access controls.
  • Helps ensure secure data discovery.
  • Supports governance and compliance.

Understanding Data Discovery in Data Catalog

Data discovery helps users find relevant data for analysis, reporting, and decision-making. For example, an analyst may search for datasets containing supply chain or operational performance data.

Using Data Catalog, users can:

  • Search data assets using keywords and metadata.
  • Filter results using available facets.
  • View metadata and schema information.
  • Access the underlying data resource, subject to permissions.

Steps to Search for Data in Data Catalog

Google Cloud Data Catalog provides a powerful search interface that allows users to quickly locate datasets across multiple Google Cloud services. Using the centralized search bar, users can explore data assets stored in platforms such as Google BigQuery and Google Cloud Pub/Sub.

Step 1: Open the Data Catalog Search Interface

Navigate to Data Catalog in the Google Cloud Console.

At the top of the interface, you will find a centralized search bar that allows users to search across all indexed data assets.

Step 2: Search and Filter Data Assets

Enter a keyword, dataset name, or table name in the Data Catalog search bar.

Use filters to narrow results by:

  • Resource type
  • Columns or schema fields
  • Metadata tags
  • Project

This helps users quickly find the required data asset.

Step 3: Explore Search Results

Once the results appear, users can explore the metadata of each data asset.

  • View descriptions and schema.
  • Check metadata tags.
  • Access the resource in services like BigQuery.
  • Understand the data structure.

Additional Data Exploration Features

Beyond basic search functionality, Data Catalog offers additional tools that help users explore and understand data assets.

  • Displays the most frequently queried Google BigQuery tables over the last 30 days.
  • Allows users to browse tables, views, and messaging topics.
  • Enables teams to apply tags for classification and governance.
  • Automatically respects source-level permissions and access controls.
